comment: The first stretch is a real climb, so take it slow and stop to catch your breath. Once you're past it the overlook is an easy stroll, and it's one of the best sunset spots near campus.
Weekend afternoons get busy. Go early, or bring a headlamp if you plan to stay for sunset.
Snap a photo of the map at the trailhead. The blue and white junctions are easy to mix up the first time around.
Every overlook has a slightly different view, so leave yourself time to stop at all seven.
Bring binoculars. Red-winged blackbirds and herons show up along the boardwalk in spring.
Completely flat and fine for strollers. A good pick when you just want some fresh air.
You can walk here straight from downtown, and it gets shady and quiet fast once you're under the trees.
The stream crossings get slick after rain, so wear shoes you don't mind getting wet.
The mountain laurel blooms here in early June. Wear orange during hunting season.
The rock fields on the ridge are slow going, so plan for more time than the mileage suggests.
It's a gentle old road grade, which makes it a good first longer hike despite the elevation gain.
The view is right at the parking lot, so it's great for sunset even if you don't feel like hiking. On a windy day you might see hang gliders.
An easy lakeside loop with the sunset reflecting off the water. A good choice for a group with mixed fitness.
Pack a swimsuit in summer. The loop is short enough to pair with a swim and a picnic.
It's stone steps the whole way up. Short, but your legs will feel it the next day. Trekking poles help on the way down.
Perfect for a lunch break. The gardens change every few weeks, so it's worth coming back.
